name: Isometric Tile World
description: A world seen from a fixed three-quarter angle: noise shapes a heightfield, the heightfield is quantised into stepped tile elevations, props are scattered on it, and the whole scene is ordered back to front and painted without a depth buffer. It shares its terrain half with the voxel compound and its input half with nothing else in the library, because pointing at a tile is a problem only a projected world has. The two contracts that carry the weight are presentation.depth_sorter, which decides what hides what, and presentation.tile_cursor, which decides what you are pointing at; both are wrong in the same way if elevation is ignored, and both are correct only if elevation is respected.

components.role: continuous surface height, before it is stepped
assigns a surface type per tile
authoritative tile store, one elevation per column
tile space to screen space, and back

the tile under the pointer, accounting for height

acceptanceCriteria: Screen and tile coordinates round-trip: projecting a tile and inverting the result returns the tile it started from, for every tile on the grid.
A pointer anywhere inside a tile's drawn diamond names that tile and no other.
The cursor names the tile a player would say they are pointing at on sloped ground, not the tile the flat inverse gives.
No object is drawn before something it hides: for every pair where one volume occludes another, the occluder is later in the draw order.
A multi-tile prop standing across an elevation change is ordered correctly against both the ground it stands on and the ground behind it.
Removing presentation.depth_sorter from the build produces a visibly wrong scene rather than a missing one, which is what makes it critical.
